New Milford at a glance

New Milford, in Litchfield County, is the largest Connecticut town by land, with 61.6 square miles. It lies about 14 miles north of Danbury on the Housatonic River and belongs to Greater Danbury and the New York metropolitan area. The 2020 census counted 28,115 residents, and the 2024 estimate is 28,334.

A town this wide has long drives between its parts. A house on a farm road in Merryall is a very different sale from one near the green, so describe the setting as well as the structure.

Villages and neighborhoods

No single neighborhood system exists here. Instead the town has named communities scattered across it: New Milford Center, Gaylordsville, Northville, Still River, Lanesville, Merryall (upper and lower), Merwinsville, Chimney Point, Park Lane, Candlewood Hills, Sunny Valley, Pickett District and Squash Hollow.

  • Gaylordsville has its own ZIP code, 06755. The rest of town uses 06776.
  • Most roads branch off U.S. 7 and U.S. 202, which cross and split inside town.
  • Communities on Candlewood Lake's northeast corner, and the rural land between Routes 7 and 202, see more visitors from May to October.

Knowing which village your house belongs to helps a buyer picture the commute and the setting. Some of the oldest housing stands near the New Milford Center Historic District, which takes in Bennitt, Elm, East, South Main, Mill and Railroad streets and is on the National Register.

Lake, rivers and wetlands

The town lies on the northeastern shore of Candlewood Lake, and the East Aspetuck, Still and Housatonic rivers all run through it. A few local offices handle questions about water.

  • Candlewood Lake Authority: 860-354-6928.
  • Inland Wetlands: 860-355-6083.
  • Health Department and sanitarian: 860-355-6035, the number to call about septic.

Own near wetlands, a river or the lake? Ask these offices what a buyer would need to know, and write down the answers.

Winter is hard on older houses here. An aging oil or propane system, a tired roof or a wet basement are the repairs that come up most often in a Litchfield County sale, and a cash buyer will not make you fix them first.

New Milford runs on a mayor-council system with a nine-member Town Council. The town has also built a 1,000,000-gallon sewer plant expansion on West Street, so the WPCA is the place to learn whether your address is on sewer.

Property tax when you sell

Under state law the seller normally settles the tax balance through the closing. Late municipal tax carries 18 percent annual interest, which is 1.5 percent per month with a $2 minimum per installment (C.G.S. 12-146).

Call the Tax Collector at 860-355-6085 for the installment dates and the figure you owe, and the Assessor at 860-355-6070 about your assessed value. Ask for the payoff to be good through your closing date so the closing attorney can pay it from the proceeds.

Conveyance tax

Connecticut charges a conveyance tax on each deed, and the seller's side handles the return. The base is three-quarters of one percent to the state and one-quarter of one percent to the town.

  • On a residential price above $800,000, the state charges a higher rate on the excess.
  • Form OP-236 goes to the town clerk at recording, and the tax is paid then.
  • Targeted investment communities may add up to one-quarter of one percent.

The Town Clerk can confirm the rate that applies to your sale.

Commuting and schools

Housatonic Area Regional Transit runs buses, and U.S. 7 and U.S. 202 are the main roads. Metro-North's Danbury Branch ends in Danbury. Tracks north of there carry freight only, and passenger service north has been discussed for years but does not exist.

The New Milford School District operates Hill and Plain, Northville, Sarah Noble Intermediate, Schaghticoke Middle and New Milford High School. Canterbury School, a Catholic boarding school, is also in town.

Wells, septic and heating on a larger lot

On a big rural lot, buyers fixate on three systems: where the water comes from, where the waste goes and what keeps the house warm. If you have a well, find the most recent water test. If you have a septic system, find out when it was last pumped and where the tank and field sit. If the house burns oil or propane, note the tank's location and age. A seller who can answer these quickly looks organized, and a seller who cannot should be ready to have the buyer price in the unknowns.

With a cash sale there is no inspection-driven repair list from a lender, but an honest description still prevents a late renegotiation.

Ways to sell

The choice is between a traditional listing and a direct cash sale, and it turns on the condition of the house and your timing.

  • A listing brings showings, a buyer's inspection and perhaps lender-driven repair requests.
  • A cash sale lets you skip repairs and pick the closing date.
  • An inherited or rural house that needs work often suits the second route.

Cash Home Buyers buys houses in New Milford in any condition. Tell us about the property and we will send an offer you can compare.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

What a cash sale leaves out

A financed buyer usually needs an appraisal, a lender's underwriting and a mortgage commitment before closing, and a problem at any of them can delay the date or lower the price. A cash buyer has none of those. You also avoid photographs, staging and weekend showings, which matter when the house is far from town or sits empty. What you give up is the chance to wait for a retail buyer, so compare the written offer with what a listing would net after repairs, commission and carrying costs.

Steps from offer to closing

  1. You accept an offer and choose a closing date.
  2. A title company or attorney orders the title search and asks your mortgage lender for a payoff letter.
  3. The Tax Collector provides the tax balance, and the WPCA confirms any sewer charge.
  4. You sign the deed, the OP-236 return and tax go to the Town Clerk, and the deed is recorded.
  5. Taxes and payoffs are subtracted from the proceeds, and you get the balance.

Bring photo ID and your latest mortgage and tax statements. For a rural house, gather what you know about the well, the septic system and the heating fuel, since a buyer will ask. If the house is an inheritance, confirm who has authority to sign before a date is set. Take your belongings out before the walk-through, and keep your insurance active until the deed is recorded.

Frequently asked questions

Is New Milford the largest town in Connecticut?

By land area, yes. It has about 61.6 square miles of land.

How do I find my New Milford tax balance before closing?

Call the Tax Collector at 860-355-6085. The office can give the amount owed so it is paid at closing.

Is there a conveyance tax when I sell in New Milford?

Yes. The base is three-quarters of one percent to the state and one-quarter of one percent to the town. The Town Clerk can confirm whether an extra municipal rate applies.

Can I sell a lakeside house near Candlewood Lake as-is?

Yes. A cash buyer purchases it in its current condition. The Candlewood Lake Authority and the Inland Wetlands office can answer waterfront questions.

Is there commuter rail in New Milford?

No. Metro-North's Danbury Branch ends in Danbury, and the tracks north of it carry freight. Local buses are run by Housatonic Area Regional Transit.

Branford at a glance

Branford sits on the Long Island Sound shoreline in New Haven County, roughly 6 miles east of New Haven, with East Haven as its western neighbor, Guilford to the east and North Branford inland. The 2020 census counted 28,273 people.

Of the town's 28.0 square miles, 6.0 are water, roughly 21.5 percent. Harbors, tidal creeks, the Branford River, Queach Brook, the Branford Supply Ponds and Lake Saltonstall all sit inside the town lines, and so do the Thimble Islands. Buyers will ask how close the house is to the water. A Branford address could be a Main Street colonial, a condominium off Brushy Plain Road or a cottage steps from a beach.

Branford villages and what each is known for

Branford works more like a string of small villages than one uniform suburb. Naming yours accurately helps a buyer picture the house.

VillageWhat a buyer will picture
Branford CenterMain Street shops and restaurants around the Town Green, with the town hall and the Branford Festival on Father's Day weekend
Branford HillThe western end along U.S. Route 1, with a commercial strip and many condominium and apartment complexes
Indian Neck and Hotchkiss GrovePeninsula and beach streets that began as summer colonies; most Hotchkiss Grove cottages are now year-round homes
Pine Orchard and Stony CreekShoreline neighborhoods toward the east, with Stony Creek built around its own harbor and the Thimble Islands cruises
Short BeachA southwest beach neighborhood with roughly 1,500 residents and several small parks

Historic districts and older houses

Seven historic districts in Branford are on the National Register of Historic Places, among them Branford Center, Branford Point, Short Beach and Stony Creek-Thimble Islands. Before planning exterior work on a house inside a district, check with the town land use office on what is allowed.

The town was settled in 1644 and incorporated in 1685, and the Harrison House and Museum dates to 1724. Plenty of the housing is old, including small cottages and second homes left from the days when the shoreline was a resort area. Tired wiring, a worn roof or an old heating system can run into real money, and that repair bill often settles whether an owner lists openly or takes a direct offer.

Getting around and why commuters look here

Interstate 95 carries most traffic, and U.S. Route 1 parallels it through the center. Route 146 is the coastal road toward Guilford, and Route 142 serves Short Beach. The Branford station is on Shore Line East, which links New London and New Haven, and Tweed New Haven Regional Airport is about 3 miles west.

Rail and the interstate both being close pulls in commuters bound for New Haven and beyond, and they are a large part of who tours a Branford house.

Moisture and weather checks before you list

About 52.6 inches of precipitation falls on Branford in a year, fairly evenly by month. Cold winters bring freeze and thaw damage and the summers are warm and humid, which is hard on roofs, gutters, basements and exterior paint.

A house near a harbor or tidal creek deserves a look at drainage and dampness before it goes on the market. Gather repair receipts, an old inspection report or a flood elevation certificate if you have them. Paperwork like that lets an investor price the house faster and with fewer surprises.

What a Branford seller owes at closing

A Connecticut conveyance tax applies once the price reaches $2,000. The seller's side generally files the return at the moment of recording, which in practice means your closing attorney or the title company deals with the town clerk.

The state share is set at three-quarters of one percent, climbing for residential estates over $800,000 and for nonresidential property. Branford's own share is one-fourth of one percent, and a town classed as a targeted investment community can add up to one-fourth of one percent more. The Branford Town Clerk can name the exact town rate for your deed.

  • Exempt transfers include a deed between spouses and a deed in lieu of foreclosure on a principal residence.
  • Selling a principal residence for less than the mortgages and liens on it may also earn an exemption from the state tax.
  • The return form is OP-236, and the town code for Branford is 014.

Property tax questions to settle before closing

Rate, installment dates and the standing of your latest bill all come from the Branford Tax Collector and Assessor.

Call the tax office before accepting an offer and ask whether any installment is past due, whether the bill will be prorated at closing, and whether liens appear on the land records. Overdue taxes, sewer charges and water bills are settled from the proceeds, and having an exact payoff number early heads off a last-minute delay.

Three ways to sell a Branford house

An owner here has three realistic routes, and each balances time, cost and certainty in its own way.

  • List with an agent: often the top asking price, in exchange for a commission, prep work, showings and a wait on the buyer's financing and inspection.
  • Sell it yourself: no commission, though pricing, paperwork, marketing and negotiating all land on you.
  • Take a direct cash offer: the buyer takes the house as it stands, so there are no repairs or showings and the closing date can bend to your schedule.

Cash works well for houses with deferred repairs, inherited homes that sit empty, owners with a moving deadline and landlords done with a tenant situation. A move-in ready house in Branford Center is a weaker fit, since it could pull several retail buyers in one weekend. We will tell you plainly which side your house falls on.

When a direct sale can fit

  • A former summer cottage in Indian Neck, Hotchkiss Grove or Short Beach that still needs work to suit year-round living.
  • An inherited house where siblings live out of state and nobody wants to manage repairs.
  • A condominium or apartment-style unit on Branford Hill whose listing has stalled.
  • A landlord who inherited a rented unit and wants to leave without a long eviction timeline.
  • A homeowner behind on payments who needs a clear closing date.

If one of these sounds familiar, send us the address and a few lines about the condition. We will explain what we can offer and what the other routes would cost you.

Frequently asked questions

How much is the Branford conveyance tax when I sell?

For most homes under $800,000 the state takes three-quarters of one percent and the town takes one-fourth of one percent. Pricier residential estates and nonresidential property pay higher tiers, and the Branford Town Clerk can confirm whether a targeted investment add-on applies.

Can I sell a Branford house with a tenant living in it?

Yes. A cash buyer can step in under the existing lease or agree on a move-out date with the tenant. Run your lease and notice rights past a Connecticut attorney before signing.

Does a historic district limit what I can do before selling in Branford?

It can. Seven Branford districts are on the National Register of Historic Places, so ask the land use office if your address is in one and whether outside changes need review.

How fast can a cash sale close in Branford?

Title work, payoff letters and the attorney's calendar set the pace. With no lender appraisal, many cash sales finish sooner than financed ones, but we will not name a date before seeing the house and the title.

Who do I call about property taxes on a Branford house?

The Tax Collector handles billing and payment status, and the Assessor gives the assessed value. Between them you can learn what is owed before closing.

Farmington at a glance

Farmington is a Hartford County town in the Farmington Valley, about 10 miles west of Hartford at a cluster of I-84 interchanges. The 2020 census counted 26,712 residents. The town covers 28.8 square miles, much of it wooded, and it shares borders with Avon, Burlington, Newington, West Hartford, Plainville, New Britain and Bristol.

For a seller, the useful part of that geography is the commute. UConn Health, Otis Worldwide and the corporate parks sit in town, so buyers who work there often want a short drive home, and a house close to the I-84 ramps tends to get a second look from them. Bradley International Airport is roughly 25 miles north.

Older houses and historic districts

Farmington was settled in 1640 and took its name in 1645, so some of its houses are very old. Main Street in the village has colonial estates, a few dating to the 1600s. The Farmington Historic District, which covers Main Street, Farmington Avenue and nearby lanes, is on the National Register of Historic Places. Unionville, in the northwest corner, grew up around factories run on Farmington River water power.

A house in either area may have older framing, original finishes or early wiring. Buyers' inspectors look hard at the foundation and the roof, and they will notice deferred work. If your property sits inside a historic district, ask the town which exterior changes need review before you pay for repairs. A cheaper route for some owners is to skip the repair list and sell as-is.

Neighborhoods buyers ask about

Farmington has one town government and several distinct communities:

  • Farmington Center and the Main Street historic district, home to Miss Porter's School.
  • Unionville, a former mill village in the northwest.
  • Bensted Corner, East Farmington Heights and Farmington Station.
  • Oakland Gardens and River Glen.

The Metacomet Ridge, a line of low traprock ridges that includes Pinnacle Rock, Rattlesnake Mountain, Farmington Mountain and Talcott Mountain, runs along the east side. Houses on slopes and ridgelines raise questions about drainage and driveway access, and an inspector will ask about both. Know your answers before the first showing.

Employers and relocation sellers

More people work in Farmington than live in it, and that shapes who buys. The town's 2024 annual financial report names UConn Health, Otis Worldwide, Companions and Homemakers, Trumpf, the town and its schools, ConnectiCare, Tunxis Community College, the American Red Cross, Connecticut Spring and Stamp, and Jackson Laboratory as its largest employers. UConn Health also houses John Dempsey Hospital, the only full-service emergency department in the Farmington Valley.

The mix has moved around. United Technologies announced in 2019 that it would shift its headquarters to Waltham, Massachusetts, and McKesson left a Farmington site that year, with about 150 jobs lost. Carvel, ConnectiCare, Farmington Displays and Horizon Technology Finance still keep headquarters here. An owner who came for one of these employers and now has to move again often needs a closing date they can count on, which is one of the situations where a cash sale gets considered.

Landmarks and trails near your lot

Farmington has a long record. In 1841, thirty-eight Mende Africans from the Amistad were housed and educated in town, and several local homes served as Underground Railroad safe houses. Well-known sites include the Hill-Stead Museum, a Colonial Revival estate completed in 1901 and a National Historic Landmark, the Stanley-Whitman House at 37 High Street, First Church of Christ at 75 Main Street, and the Gridley-Parsons-Staples Homestead at 1554 Farmington Avenue.

The Farmington Canal once linked New Haven with Northampton, Massachusetts, and ran between 1828 and 1848. A railroad later used the right of way, with parts active into the 1990s, and sections are now the Farmington Canal Heritage Trail and the Farmington River Trail. If your lot touches a trail, read the plat and deed for easements before you describe a boundary to a buyer.

Conveyance tax and recording

Connecticut wants the conveyance tax return filed and the tax paid before a deed is recorded. Section 12-497 of the General Statutes bars a town clerk from recording a taxable deed until that happens, so the payment is part of every closing, whether you list or sell for cash.

Section 12-494 sets the base charge at three-quarters of one percent for the state and one-fourth of one percent for the town. Non-residential property and residential sales above $800,000 carry higher state rates. The statute pages carry a 2026 Supplement, so confirm the current rate with your closing attorney before you plan on a net figure.

Property tax is a separate matter. Chapter 204 of the General Statutes covers installments, interest and liens, and any unpaid balance is usually settled from the sale proceeds at closing.

Schools and getting around

Farmington Public Schools run four pre-K to grade 4 schools (Union, West District, Noah Wallace and East Farms), West Woods Upper Elementary for grades 5 and 6, Irving A. Robbins Middle School for grades 7 and 8, and Farmington High School. Miss Porter's School, a private day and boarding school founded in 1843, fills much of the village center, and Tunxis Community College is in the southwest. I-84 is the main road, and CT Transit Hartford runs local buses.

How a Farmington cash sale moves

The first step is a conversation about the house: age, condition, who is on the title and whether anyone lives there. A buyer then makes a written offer. Because nothing depends on a lender's appraisal, the remaining work is title search, the conveyance tax return and the closing itself.

Bring the deed, your most recent property tax bill, any mortgage payoff statement and, for an estate, the paperwork showing who may sign. If there is a tenant, bring the lease. Having these ready is what shortens the timeline, and a closing attorney can tell you early if a lien or an old easement needs clearing first.

Listing versus a cash sale

A cash sale fits when time, condition or paperwork is the obstacle. Typical Farmington cases include an inherited colonial that needs updating, a house with a tenant, or a seller relocating for work at one of the corporate campuses.

  • Listing: more exposure, but showings, inspections and financing contingencies.
  • Cash sale: the buyer takes the house as-is, and the timeline is driven by title work.

Whichever route you pick, have your closing attorney review the contract, and keep a written copy of every offer so you can compare them side by side.

Where is Farmington, CT?

Farmington is in Hartford County, about 10 miles west of Hartford in the Farmington Valley, at a hub of I-84 interchanges.

What is Unionville, CT?

Unionville is a village in the northwest corner of Farmington that grew around factories powered by the Farmington River. It belongs to the town and keeps its own identity.

Who is the largest employer in Farmington?

UConn Health, with 7,664 employees in the town's 2024 financial report, followed by Otis Worldwide with 4,077.

Do I pay conveyance tax when I sell a house in Farmington?

Connecticut charges a tax on deeds worth $2,000 or more, split between the state and the town. Ask your closing attorney for the current rate for your price and property type.

Can I sell an older Farmington house as-is?

Yes. A cash buyer purchases the house in its current condition, which suits older homes with deferred repairs. Compare any offer in writing and have it reviewed before you sign.

Westport at a glance

Westport is a Fairfield County town on Long Island Sound, about 48 miles northeast of New York City in the stretch people call the Gold Coast. The 2020 census counted 27,141 residents. Of its 33.45 square miles, only 19.96 are land, since 13.49 are water, and the center of town stands just 26 feet above sea level. Norwalk lies to the west, Weston to the north, Wilton to the northwest and Fairfield to the east.

Interstate 95, the Merritt Parkway and US Route 1 all cross town, and Metro-North's New Haven Line stops at Westport and Greens Farms. Amtrak does not stop here, so riders go to Bridgeport or Stamford. Commuter access helps sell a house, so mention it in your description.

Westport neighborhoods

The town has more than ten named areas, ranging from a downtown village to separate shoreline communities. Knowing the right name for yours helps a buyer place the house at once.

AreaWhat to know
SaugatuckAround the railroad station, with restaurants, shops and offices

Old Hill, Coleytown, Poplar Plains and Staples are older, inland areas. An owner on Saugatuck Island may see a separate charge on the tax bill, so ask the tax collector what applies to your address.

Floodplain rules and renovations

About 26 percent of Westport residents, and the train station, are inside the 100-year floodplain. The floodplain was breached in 1992 and 1996, which damaged private property and flooded the station parking lot.

The town has put flood mitigation measures in place since then, including regulations that govern renovations and additions in the floodplain zone. A flood-zone lot may therefore limit how much you or a buyer can build or rebuild. Ask the town's building and zoning staff about your lot and check the FEMA map before you promise a buyer anything. Your insurance policy will tell you whether flood coverage is already in place.

What taxes and paperwork apply when you sell?

The seller or the seller's attorney files Connecticut Form OP-236, the conveyance tax return, with the Westport town clerk when the deed is recorded. The Department of Revenue Services requires it on transfers of $2,000 or more unless an exemption applies. Westport's town code on the form is 158.

Towns that take part in the state's myCTREC system accept the filing electronically. Others accept the paper form. On a Westport sale the dollar amount of the return can be large, so double-check the price and the code with your attorney before you sign.

  • Ask the tax collector for current balances, including any special district charge.
  • Ask the town about floodplain rules if the lot is near the river or shore.
  • Confirm who pays the escrow or closing items listed in your contract.

Call those offices directly for answers on your parcel.

Common Westport situations

Sellers can list with an agent, sell privately or accept a cash offer. The best choice usually turns on the house's condition and the timeline.

  • Older houses that need updating before a financed buyer can close.
  • Flood-zone lots where renovation is restricted.
  • Estates that must clear title before a sale.
  • Owners moving on a short schedule.

A cash offer can remove the lender appraisal step, though you should compare it with what a listing would net after commission and repairs. Send us the address and a short description of the house, and we will explain what a cash purchase could look like in Westport before you decide anything.

Selling a house with flood or renovation limits

If your lot has restrictions, a buyer's lender or insurer may ask whether the house can be insured and rebuilt after damage. Gather the elevation or flood zone paperwork you already have, along with any permits for past additions and a list of repairs after storms.

A buyer paying cash may be more relaxed about those limits, but the price will reflect them. Neither a listing nor a cash sale makes the rules disappear, so your best protection is knowing the facts and telling every buyer the same thing.

How a cash purchase differs from a listing

On the market, you prepare the house, wait for showings, negotiate repairs after an inspection and then wait again while the buyer's bank finishes its review. A cash purchase compresses that. The buyer looks at the house as it is, makes a single offer and does not need a loan, so the main gating item becomes your title work.

That speed has a cost, which is why the comparison matters. Ask yourself what a listing would honestly bring after the agent's fee, the work an inspector would flag and the months of carrying a large house. Westport carrying costs are real, and they keep running while a sign is in the yard.

Estates, heirs and shared ownership

Inherited houses are among the most common cash sales anywhere. If several heirs own the property, all of them usually need to agree before a deed is signed, and the person named to act for the estate must show proof of that authority. Start collecting those documents early, because a missing signature can hold up an otherwise simple closing.

It also helps to decide who will handle keys, utilities and insurance while the sale is underway. A vacant house still needs heat in winter and regular checks, and the policy may change once the owner has died, so call the insurer.

Papers worth locating now

A little digging before the first call pays off later. Look for the deed, the most recent tax bill, any mortgage statement and the homeowner's insurance declarations page. If you ever had a survey, the certificate of occupancy or a permit for work on the house, add those. Where the house sits near water, any flood certificate or elevation record belongs in the same folder.

None of these is required to start a conversation, and a missing paper is rarely a deal breaker. The folder simply lets a buyer move quickly, and shows that you have nothing to hide.

Preparing for the closing

  1. Request a written tax balance from the collector, and ask whether any special district charge applies.
  2. If you have a mortgage, order the payoff statement close to the closing date.
  3. Walk the house once more with the buyer and agree on what stays.
  4. Sign the deed and the conveyance return, and make sure the town clerk records both.
  5. Collect your closing statement and keep it with your tax records.

With an inherited house, the person who can legally sign should see these steps at the start.

Part of it is. About 26 percent of residents and the train station sit in the 100-year floodplain. Check the FEMA map and ask the town about your specific lot.

What is Westport's town code for the conveyance tax form?

It is 158 on Connecticut Form OP-236. The seller or the seller's attorney files the form when the deed is recorded.

Yes. You can sell without making repairs, though you should disclose known issues and expect any buyer to price them in. A cash buyer may purchase the house in its present condition.

Newtown at a glance

Newtown is a northern Fairfield County town, roughly 45 miles southwest of Hartford and 42 miles northeast of New York City. It is part of Greater Danbury and the Western Connecticut Planning Region. The 2020 census found 27,173 residents spread over roughly 58 square miles of land, which makes it the fifth largest town in the state by area.

Outside the central borough, local zoning sets a minimum lot of one acre, so most houses here sit on bigger parcels than a coastal city offers. The Housatonic River forms the northeastern border.

Post-war houses and what they need

English colonists bought the townsite in 1705, and Newtown was incorporated in 1711. After World War II the town turned into a Danbury suburb, with commuters also heading to Norwalk, Stamford and Bridgeport. Population went from 7,448 in 1950 to 16,942 in 1970 and 25,031 in 2000.

The houses from that growth are decades old now. An owner who does not want to replace a septic system, furnace or roof before listing can look for a buyer who takes the house as it stands.

Villages inside Newtown

Newtown has no single downtown. It is organized around villages: Botsford, Dodgingtown, Hattertown, Hawleyville, Sandy Hook and the Newtown Borough, plus smaller areas such as Taunton, Head of Meadow, Huntingtown and Middle Gate.

  • Newtown Borough, Hawleyville and Botsford share ZIP code 06470.
  • Sandy Hook, which includes Berkshire, Riverside, Walnut Tree Hill and Zoar, uses ZIP code 06482.

Name your village to a buyer. It tells them about the commute, the school zone and the lot size to expect.

The Borough of Newtown

The Borough is a small separate municipality inside the town, about 1,252 acres in the center and one of only nine boroughs in Connecticut. The General Assembly incorporated it in 1824.

Services differ inside its lines. The Borough has public water through the Water and Sewer Authority, and much of it is sewered. Most of the rest of Newtown relies on private wells and septic systems, and borough zoning allows lots smaller than the one-acre minimum used elsewhere.

Outside the Borough, expect a buyer to ask about the age and condition of your well and septic system. Those two items often drive repair negotiations on rural Connecticut sales.

Property tax in Newtown

Real estate tax is billed in two installments, July and January, on a mill rate of 29.26 for the 2025 Grand List. A bill under $50 is due in one installment in July.

InstallmentDueLast day without penalty
FirstJulyAugust 1, unless it falls on a weekend
SecondJanuaryFebruary 1, unless it falls on a weekend

Delinquent tax carries 18% interest a year, which is 1.5% a month with a $2 minimum per installment. A mailed payment is on time if postmarked by the last day to pay.

The Tax Collector also bills sewer and water use charges and benefit assessments, so a final balance check before closing should cover those. The office number is 203-270-4320. To estimate an annual bill, multiply the assessed value by the mill rate and divide by 1,000.

Conveyance tax at closing

The state attaches a tax to the deed when a Newtown house changes hands. Base rates put three-quarters of one percent in Hartford's hands and one-quarter of one percent in the town's.

  • Any slice of a residential price above $800,000 is taxed at a steeper state rate.
  • Form OP-236 is filed at recording by the grantor, or by the grantor's attorney or agent.
  • Some transfers are exempt, among them a transfer between spouses and a deed in lieu of foreclosure on a principal residence.

Targeted investment communities may layer on as much as one more quarter of one percent. The Newtown Town Clerk is the person to ask whether anything sits on top of the base rate.

Town government, permits and schools

A First Selectman and a Board of Selectmen lead the town. A 12-member Legislative Council passes ordinances and approves budgets, and the final budget goes to a town-wide referendum. A seller feels this only when a project is pending, such as an open permit, a zoning question or an unfinished addition. Check with the town offices about open permits before you sign, because an unresolved one can hold up a conventional closing.

Newtown Public Schools runs four elementary schools (Hawley, Head O'Meadow, Middle Gate and Sandy Hook), Reed Intermediate for grades 5 and 6, Newtown Middle School for grades 7 and 8, and Newtown High School. Know which elementary school your street feeds, since buyers ask.

Which sale route fits

How much preparation you can face usually decides it: list with an agent, or sell to a cash buyer.

  • Listing: best when the house is in good condition and you can wait for the right offer.
  • Cash: better for an estate, a house with tenants, or a property with a failing septic system or other deferred work.
  • Cash Home Buyers purchases Newtown houses as they stand, with no repairs required first.

Ask us for a cash offer with no strings, then set it against an agent's estimate for your address.

Septic and well questions at sale time

If your property has a private well, find the latest water test. If it has a septic system, find the last pumping record and note where the tank and leach field are. Missing paperwork is common on older houses, and a buyer may ask for an inspection. A failing system is not the end of a sale, but it affects the price, and a cash buyer will count the repair into the offer instead of asking you to fund it first.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

If taxes or sewer charges are unpaid

An unpaid balance is not a roadblock. The Tax Collector bills sewer and water use charges and benefit assessments along with the tax, so ask for one total that covers all of them through your closing date. The title company subtracts it from your proceeds. Because delinquent interest builds each month, a payoff letter that has gone stale understates what you owe, and a new one costs nothing but a phone call.

Keep the letter with your closing papers. If an estate or a co-owner is involved, make sure everyone with a name on the title can be reached before a date is set.

From accepted offer to closing

  1. You accept an offer and choose a closing date.
  2. A title company or attorney searches the title and orders a payoff from your lender.
  3. You confirm your final tax and sewer or water balance with the Tax Collector.
  4. You sign the deed, Form OP-236 and the tax are submitted at recording, and you receive what is left after payoffs.

Bring photo ID and your recent mortgage and tax statements. Empty the house, leave keys and openers, and keep your homeowner's policy in force until the deed is recorded. If an estate is selling, settle early who has authority to sign.

Frequently asked questions

How high is the Newtown mill rate?

29.26 on the 2025 Grand List. To estimate a yearly bill, multiply assessed value by that rate and divide by 1,000.

When are Newtown property taxes due?

You can pay in July and January. Penalty-free deadlines are normally August 1 and February 1, pushed back when either lands on a weekend.

Do Newtown houses use septic systems and wells?

Many do. Public water serves the Borough, which is also largely sewered, while the rest of town mostly depends on wells and septic.

What conveyance tax applies to a Newtown sale?

Base rates are three-quarters of one percent for the state and one-quarter for the town. Form OP-236 is filed at recording, and the Town Clerk knows about any added municipal rate.

Can I sell a Newtown house with a failing septic system?

Yes. A cash buyer takes the house as-is, so the system does not have to be replaced beforehand. Expect the price to reflect the repair.

New London in a few lines

New London is a harbor city where the Thames River meets Long Island Sound, in the Southeastern Connecticut Planning Region. Of its 10.59 square miles, 5.61 are land and 4.98 are water, so almost half the city is wet. The U.S. Coast Guard Academy, Connecticut College, Mitchell College and The Williams School are all here.

The city dates to 1646 and was incorporated in 1784. Whaling wealth paid for much of the 19th-century architecture that still stands, and an older house in a port city of this vintage can hide old wiring, plumbing and masonry. Buyers who rely on a mortgage often ask for repairs on such houses, while a cash sale skips that step.

Numbers for sellers

MeasureValue
Population, 2020 census27,367 (28,003 estimated for 2025)
Households, 202010,724
Housing units, 202012,119, with 11.5% vacant
Median household income, 2018 to 2022$56,237
Mill rate, 2025 grand list27.10

About 39.4 percent of households were one person in 2020.

Property tax and payoffs

New London bills real estate tax in two installments, due July 1 and January 1. Every bill is mailed in June, with copies enough for both installments, and no second real estate or personal property bill follows. The second installment can be printed from the city's online tax portal.

Each installment has a grace period through the first day of the following month. The January 1, 2027 installment can be paid without penalty through Monday, February 1, 2027. Delinquent tax collects interest at 1.5 percent a month, and state statute sets a $2.00 minimum.

  • Mill rate on the 2025 grand list: 27.10 for real estate, personal property and motor vehicles.
  • City Center District: a separate 0.99 mill rate on the 2025 grand list.
  • Office: 15 Masonic Street, behind City Hall, Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Phone (860) 447-5208.

The collector wants owners to tell the Assessor about a new mailing address when they buy, move or pay off a mortgage. When you sell, ask for a payoff that covers both installments through the closing date.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your New London house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Fort Trumbull and redevelopment

Fort Trumbull is where the city's best-known property fight began. New London used eminent domain to take nearly two dozen homes, and the U.S. Supreme Court upheld the taking in Kelo v. City of New London, decided 5 to 4 in 2005. The homes came down for a development plan whose developer never found financing.

The lesson for an owner is simple. Near the waterfront or a redevelopment area, call the city's planning office and ask what is proposed. Whatever you learn, pass it along to a buyer.

Storms, water and the house

Hurricanes have reached the Connecticut coast only now and then, but with force: landfalls in 1903, 1938, 1944, 1954 (Carol), 1960 (Donna) and 1985 (Gloria). Tropical Storm Irene in 2011 and Hurricane Sandy in 2012 did moderate damage along the shore. Three habits help a seller.

  • Ask your insurer about flood zone status for the lot, since a buyer's lender will.
  • Look over the roof, siding and windows for wind and salt wear.
  • Write down past water damage and what was repaired.

Transit, ferries and the military

I-95 runs through the city. New London Union Station, designed by H.H. Richardson, has Amtrak's Northeast Regional and Shore Line East. Buses come from Southeast Area Transit, Estuary Transit District and Greyhound. The Cross Sound Ferry to Long Island, the Fishers Island Ferry and the Block Island Ferry all depart here, and the State Pier is being converted for offshore wind.

The Naval Submarine Base New London is across the river in Groton, and the Coast Guard Academy is inside the city. An owner moving on military or Coast Guard orders may need a closing date that matches them, and a cash sale can sometimes meet a tight date.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy New London houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Connecticut conveyance tax

Deeds with $2,000 or more of consideration are taxed. Recording is blocked at the clerk's office until the return and payment are in.

  • State share on a house: 0.75 percent up to $800,000, 1.25 percent up to $2,500,000, then 2.25 percent.
  • Municipal share: 0.25 percent.
  • A certified pyrrhotite foundation can exempt the first sale of a principal residence.

A targeted investment community may add up to one-fourth of one percent more. Your contract and closing attorney say who pays.

Selling fast

Most owners put a listing next to a cash sale. A listing reaches more buyers and brings showings, appraisals and repair requests.

  • As-is cash sale: no lender, no repair list, and a closing date set with the title company.
  • Inherited house: confirm who has authority to sign and whether probate steps are needed.
  • Back taxes: get a payoff from the tax collector so the offer and the closing figures agree.

Confirm legal and tax questions with a Connecticut attorney or the city office.

Preparing an older house for any buyer

Whether you list or sell for cash, a short walk-through before you talk price pays off. Check the attic and basement for moisture, look at the electrical panel and any visible wiring, and note which systems are original. Gather permits, receipts and warranties for work done over the years. A buyer who sees paperwork tends to trust the rest of what you say.

If back taxes are owed, there is no need to pay first and sell second. The title company counts them against the proceeds, which is why the written payoff matters. Keep a copy of it and bring it to the closing.

One more habit helps. Keep every message with the buyer, the title company and the city in one folder, on paper or on your phone, so a question about a date or a figure can be answered in minutes rather than hunted down.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

How a closing unfolds

  1. You accept an offer and agree on a closing date with the buyer.
  2. A title company or attorney searches the title and clears anything that blocks a clean deed.
  3. Your mortgage lender sends a payoff letter, and the tax collector provides the tax figure.
  4. You sign the deed, the return goes to the town clerk, and you are paid what remains after payoffs.

Bring photo ID and your latest loan and tax statements. If a co-owner or an estate representative has to sign, line that up early. Remove your belongings before the walk-through, and cancel or transfer utilities for the closing date. Do not skip the last step of keeping insurance in force until the deed is recorded.

Frequently asked questions

What is the mill rate in New London, CT?

For the 2025 grand list it is 27.10 for real estate, personal property and motor vehicles, plus 0.99 in the City Center District. Confirm the current figure with the tax collector.

When are New London real estate taxes due?

July 1 and January 1. The January 1, 2027 installment can be paid without penalty through Monday, February 1, 2027.

Does New London mail a second tax bill?

No. Bills go out in June with copies for each installment, and the second can be printed from the online tax portal.

What interest does New London charge on late taxes?

Delinquent tax accrues interest at 1.5 percent a month, with a $2.00 minimum under state statute.

How big is the conveyance tax on a New London house?

On a house up to $800,000 the base combined rate is 1 percent, 0.75 percent state and 0.25 percent municipal. The state rate climbs on the portion above $800,000.

East Haven in brief

East Haven is a New Haven County shoreline town about 3 miles east of New Haven, with Long Island Sound along its southern edge. It covers 13.4 square miles, 1.2 of them water, and had 27,923 residents in 2020. It is about 35 miles from Hartford and 82 miles from New York City.

The map shows a town that is taller than it is wide. New Haven is on the west, North Haven on the north, and Branford, North Branford and Lake Saltonstall on the east. East Haven shares Tweed New Haven Airport and the Alling Memorial Golf Course with New Haven, and Stony Island lies offshore from the town beach.

The three sections of East Haven

Residents think in three big sections, not dozens of small neighborhoods, and each draws different buyer questions.

  • Foxon: the hilliest part, north and east around State Route 80, home to the high school and Foxon Park Beverage.
  • Momauguin: the southern shore, with the town beach, condominiums, summer cottages and an industrial park by the airport.
  • The Center: Town Hall, fire department headquarters, Hagaman Memorial Library and the Old Stone Church of 1774, plus the West End next to New Haven.

A shore cottage in Momauguin, a hillside house in Foxon and an older West End house are three different sales. Tell us which section you are in, since it affects how we think about the price and who might want the house.

Storms, snow and flood questions

Long Island Sound tempers the weather, so winters are milder and snow lighter than inland, with about 27 inches in a normal winter and 45.1 inches of precipitation a year. Storms still matter if you own near the water. Hurricane Gloria in 1985 left the area without electricity, phone and cable for 7 days, and Hurricane Irene in August 2011 destroyed houses along Cosey Beach. Nor'easters can bring heavy rain or snow, and the Blizzard of 1978 dropped almost 2 feet.

Waterside sellers should expect buyers and insurers to ask about flood exposure. Find out the flood zone for your lot from the town, and gather any elevation certificate or insurance history.

Roads, rail and services

Interstate 95 crosses the middle of town with U.S. Route 1 beside it through the Center. State Routes 80, 100 and 142 also run through, and Route 80 crosses Foxon east to west.

There is no train station in East Haven. Union Station in New Haven, with Amtrak, is about 3 miles from the center, and a commuter station in Branford is the same distance. Connecticut Transit buses serve the town. Yale New Haven Hospital and related facilities are 3 to 5 miles away in New Haven, since the town has no hospital of its own.

Utilities for closing

Regional providers serve East Haven, so closing paperwork often touches several accounts.

  • Water: the Regional Water Authority, from Lake Saltonstall in the south and Lake Gaillard in the north
  • Sewage: the New Haven Regional Water Pollution Control Authority
  • Electric: United Illuminating
  • Natural gas: Southern Connecticut Gas, with local propane distributors in some sections

On a propane house, ask the supplier about a final reading and who owns the tank before closing.

East Haven property tax and mill rate

The 2025 Grand List taxes real estate and personal property at 35.78 mills and motor vehicles at 32.46 mills. The first installment is due July 1 with grace into August, and the second falls in January 2027. Only one bill goes out a year, even when it is paid in two installments.

Assessments and revaluation

The Assessor values every real, personal and motor vehicle property and files the Grand List with the Town Clerk by January 31 and with the state by May 1. Connecticut requires a town-wide revaluation every five years.

A 2026 revaluation is on file with the assessor. New values change the tax a buyer will carry, so call 203-468-3233 for the status and the appeal steps. The office is at 250 Main Street, upper level of Town Hall.

Preparing a shore-area house for sale

Buyers near the water ask the same few questions, so answer them in advance. Which flood zone is the lot in? Is there an elevation certificate? What does insurance cost and has the house ever had a claim? Did Irene, or any storm since, damage it, and what was fixed?

Photographs and receipts for storm repairs carry weight. So does a clear statement of what is still undone. A buyer who sees a deferred roof or a damaged porch priced fairly is usually less nervous than one who finds it later.

For a hillside house in Foxon, the questions shift to drainage and heating. For a West End house, they turn to age and updates. Either way, the more you know before the first showing, the steadier the negotiation. Write the answers down and keep them with your tax and utility papers.

Conveyance tax filing

The return goes in at recording, from the seller or the seller's attorney, and tax is due on prices of $2,000 or more unless an exemption applies. East Haven is town code 044 on the state's list.

  • A transfer between spouses is exempt.
  • A principal residence sold for less than the mortgages and priority taxes owed on it can be exempt.
  • A deed in lieu of foreclosure on a principal residence can be exempt.

Your closing attorney sets the amount and the codes. Ask early, since the return goes with the deed. The closing attorney can also tell you who files and pays at the table.

A cash sale in East Haven

A shore cottage needing storm repairs, an older house, an inherited house or a loan that has fallen behind: a cash sale takes any of them as they stand.

When are East Haven taxes due?

The first installment is due July 1, with payment accepted without penalty into August. Bills of $200 or more can be split, and the second installment comes due in January 2027.

Is East Haven's flood risk a concern when selling?

It can be. The town sits on Long Island Sound, and Hurricane Irene destroyed houses along Cosey Beach in 2011, so buyers often ask about flood zone and insurance.

Can I sell an East Haven house that has storm damage?

Yes. A cash buyer can take a house as it stands, damage and deferred repairs included.

Wethersfield at a glance

Immediately south of Hartford, on the Connecticut River, Wethersfield belongs to Hartford County and the Capitol Planning Region. The town measures about 13.1 square miles, roughly 12.3 of them land, and counted 27,298 people in 2020. English settlers arrived in October 1634, and the town was incorporated on February 21, 1637, alongside Windsor and Hartford. It still calls itself "Ye Most Ancient Town in Connecticut." The ZIP code is 06109.

Interstate 91 serves the town at exits 25 and 26, and Route 99, the Silas Deane Highway, is the main commercial road. Others include Route 175 (Wells Road), Route 287 (Prospect Street), Route 15 and US Route 5, and Route 3 over the Putnam Bridge. CT Transit runs routes 43, 47, 53, 55, 61 and 91 here, and Hartford station is the closest passenger rail stop. Many buyers look at Wethersfield because Hartford is right next door.

Old Wethersfield and older houses

The National Register added Old Wethersfield as a historic district in 1970. Spread over about two square miles, it holds roughly 1,100 buildings from the 17th, 18th and 19th centuries, which makes it the largest historic district in Connecticut. Three buildings are listed as landmarks on their own: the Buttolph-Williams House on Broad Street, the Joseph Webb House at 211 Main Street and the Silas Deane House at 203 Main Street.

Inside the district, expect buyers to ask about the age of the house, its original windows and prior alterations. Older framing, knob and tube wiring, oil heat and stone foundations come up often. Outside it, most of the housing is from the 20th century, but deferred maintenance is common there too. Ask the town's building office which permits are on file for your address before you list. A missing permit for a finished basement or a replaced furnace can stall a conventional closing.

Assessment, mill rate and the phase-in

The assessment year runs from October 1 to September 30. Wethersfield finished a state-mandated revaluation for the October 1, 2024 Grand List, and the Town Council adopted a four-year phase-in of the new values. Under it, an increase in assessment is stepped up in equal parts each year until the full new value applies.

For a buyer, that means the tax bill can keep climbing during the remaining phase-in years even if the mill rate stays put. Anyone comparing offers should ask the assessor's office for the current phased assessment on the specific parcel.

How does the conveyance tax work when a Wethersfield house closes?

A deed recorded in Connecticut brings a conveyance tax, and the return comes from the seller's side. Form OP-236 is submitted by the grantor, the grantor's attorney or an authorized agent for any price of $2,000 or more that no exemption covers. On the form, Wethersfield is town code 159.

One exemption helps owners who are underwater: a principal residence sold for less than the mortgages plus the real estate taxes and municipal liens that rank ahead of them. Rates and the town's share shift over time, so get the current figures from the clerk or your attorney.

Flood and water risk near the river

Wethersfield grew on the Connecticut River floodplain, and the 1936 flood is part of its history. Great Meadows and Wethersfield Cove sit along the river. Not every house is affected, yet a lender will usually check flood zone status for riverside and low-lying addresses.

Check your parcel's flood zone with the town and on the FEMA map before you decide how to sell. A basement that has seen water should be on your list of disclosures.

What Wethersfield sellers usually run into

Typical calls involve deferred repairs on old houses, inherited homes with several heirs, and owners who have fallen behind on taxes or a mortgage. In a town with this much historic building stock, repair lists can run long.

  • Roof, chimney or window work on a house built before 1900.
  • A basement or foundation that has seen water, which matters near the river and the Cove.
  • Heirs who live out of state and cannot agree on a list price.
  • Tax or lien balances that must be paid from sale proceeds.
  • Tenants in a multi-family house who are not cooperative on showings.

When a house passes to a family, every owner on title normally has to sign the deed. Brothers and sisters in different states may disagree on a price, or one may want to keep the place while another wants cash. Disagreement over price is common, and an outside number can help. A cash offer and a listing estimate side by side often turn a vague argument into a plain comparison that everyone can read.

On closing day you sign the deed, the closing attorney pays off any mortgage, tax or lien from the money, and the deed is recorded with the town clerk along with the conveyance return. Start a folder before any buyer visits. If a payoff or lien turns up, get the amount in writing and drop it in the folder. A title search is coming regardless, and the more you already know, the fewer odd lines show on the closing statement.

The seller, the seller's attorney or an authorized agent files Form OP-236 when the deed is recorded and the price is $2,000 or more. Wethersfield's town code on the form is 159.

South Windsor basics

South Windsor is a Hartford County town on the east bank of the Connecticut River, with 26,918 residents at the 2020 census. Old Main Street runs near the river and anchors the oldest part of town, and newer subdivisions, shopping areas and industrial parks lie farther east. A nine-member Town Council meets at 1540 Sullivan Avenue.

The town went from 4,066 people in 1950 to 15,553 in 1970, and most of the houses from that wave are now 50 to 70 years old. That is the age when roofs, boilers, windows and septic or sewer connections tend to need money. An owner of one of those houses often has to decide whether to fund the work or sell without it.

Older homes and historic listings

Three places are on the National Register of Historic Places: the East Windsor Hill Historic District, the Elmore Houses on Long Hill Road and the Windsor Farms Historic District. If your house is an older one near Main Street, ask the town's land use staff what rules apply before planning exterior changes. Historic status can limit what a buyer is allowed to do, and buyers will ask.

The Connecticut River and the Scantic River border parts of town, so check flood zone status for your parcel with your insurer or lender. Commuters will care about the roads, because U.S. Route 5 and Interstate 291 follow the western edge of town beside the river, so say how long your drive to them takes.

Winter damage to watch for

Winters are cold, with record lows of minus 24 degrees, and rain falls in every month. Freeze and thaw cycles work on driveways, chimneys, foundations and roof flashing, and steady moisture makes basements and crawl spaces a common inspection issue.

A vacant or inherited house is the most exposed. Pipes that are not winterized can burst, and a house left unheated for one winter loses value quickly. Keep the utilities on and the roof tight until the sale closes.

Public school students attend one of four elementary schools (Pleasant Valley, Orchard Hill, Philip R. Smith and Eli Terry), then Timothy Edwards Middle School, then South Windsor High School. Buyers with children ask which school serves a street, so put the answer in your notes.

Many buyers at these price points use conventional financing and ask for repairs after the inspection. Some sellers choose a cash sale to skip that step. Connecticut puts this tax on the seller whenever a deed carries $2,000 or more in consideration. The town gets its own 0.25 percent too. Commercial property other than unimproved land pays the state 1.25 percent. The governing law is Chapter 223, Sec. 12-494.

A town with certain qualifying conditions may add a little more, which is a question for the clerk. Some transfers owe nothing, such as a principal residence handed over in lieu of foreclosure, or a sale whose price falls short of the mortgages and the tax liens ranked ahead of them.

What happens at recording

On closing day the deed is recorded, and Form OP-236 goes in with it. The seller, the seller's lawyer or an authorized agent can sign and file the form, and payment is due right then. In towns on the myCTREC system the payment can be made online, with the bank draft starting only once the instrument has been recorded. Property tax billing and late interest

South Windsor, like every Connecticut town, picks its own billing plan: one, two or four installments. The statute only demands that the last one come due at least 45 days ahead of the end of the fiscal year (Chapter 204, Sec. 12-142). If an installment goes unpaid it turns delinquent, and interest of 18 percent a year starts to run, with a floor of $2 per installment unless the town waives it (Sec. 12-146).

The Collector of Revenue can give you the real dates and the mill rate, and the Assessor can answer questions about the assessment. Ask the Collector whether a sewer or other municipal charge is open against the parcel. Knowing that before closing keeps the payoff figure right.

When a cash sale suits a worn house

A buyer paying cash does not need a bank appraisal and is not bound by a lender's repair list. An old roof, a tired septic or sewer connection or years of deferred upkeep are therefore not the obstacle they are on a financed sale. The buyer prices in the work, so the check will usually be lower than what a renovated house might bring on the open market.

If your house is in good shape and you can wait several months, a listing may pay more. When speed, privacy or certainty count most, cash is the better fit. We buy South Windsor houses, and others in nearby Hartford County towns, as they stand, and we will walk you through our figure so you can set it beside a listing.

Tenants, liens and where to start

Plenty of houses sell with a tenant living there or a lien on file. Closing pays off a past-due tax or lien from your proceeds, and the buyer should hear about a tenant at the outset. A Connecticut attorney can say how a lease and your timetable fit together.

Begin with three documents: the deed, your current mortgage statement and the latest tax bill. Request the tax balance from the Collector of Revenue, hire a closing attorney, and then compare offers using real figures before you set a date.

On the day itself, take photo ID and all the keys. Your lawyer will go through the closing statement with you line by line, so you can see every payoff before you sign. Ask about anything that looks unfamiliar, and ask for a copy of the final statement to keep with your records.

Hartford County, on the Connecticut River's east bank. About 26,918 people lived there at the 2020 census.

The seller owes it. It is collected when the deed gets recorded, at 0.75 percent to the state and 0.25 percent to the town, with a higher state rate above $800,000 on residential sales.

What do I pay if a property tax installment is late?

Interest of 18 percent a year, counted from the original due date, once the installment is delinquent. Each installment carries a $2 minimum unless the town waives it.

Does a lien or a tenant block a sale here?

Not usually. Liens come out of the proceeds at closing, and tenants should be mentioned to the buyer right away. Ask a Connecticut attorney about your situation.

No. Cash buyers purchase the house as it is, so the repairs only affect the price offered.

Connecticut has a specific conveyance tax exemption for a principal residence with a deteriorating concrete foundation caused by pyrrhotite, as determined by a professional engineer. Ledge, drainage and wells

Ridgefield sits on uneven bedrock. Ledge, steep driveways and runoff are the things inspectors and buyers tend to ask about on a hilly lot, and a seller who already has the answers moves faster.

Before you list or take an offer, walk the property after a hard rain. Look at the gutters, the grading beside the foundation and the sump pump, and write down any time water has reached the basement. Buyers ask, and a straight answer reads better than a surprise found during inspection.

Winter is hard on pipes and roofs. If the house will sit empty, keep the heat on, and keep records of any recent roof or furnace work so you can hand them over.

The rate depends on the price and can change, so get the exact figure from your closing attorney or the town clerk. For an assessment dispute or a tax balance, call the assessor or the tax collector.

  5. Hire a closing attorney, who will order the title search and prepare the deed and the conveyance tax return.
  6. Keep the utilities on until the day of closing, then arrange final readings.

On closing day, bring a government photo ID, every key and garage opener, and the paperwork for any warranties still in force. If taxes or a lien are owed, the payoff is taken from your proceeds at the table, so the earlier you know the amount, the fewer delays you will have.

What a cash sale skips

A traditional listing usually means cleaning, staging, showings, a buyer's mortgage approval and a repair negotiation after the inspection. A cash sale can drop most of those steps.
